To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rare earth elements in the blood serum samples of the patients with various diseases were determined by inductively-coupled plasma mass spectrometric analysis, where the blood samples were digested with nitro acid and perchlorate acid, and then the rare earth elements were concentrated by chelating resin, and then determined by ICP-MS.
the concentrations of all rare earth element in human blood serum are at the ppt ( 10−12 g/ ml) level.
the concentrations of REEs in human blood serum are at the ppt level, which is the same level of the concentrations of REs in human blood serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the multielement determination for the rare earth elements in the human blood serum.

the determination of rare earth elements (La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu, and Y) in human blood serum samples by inductively-coupled plasma mass spectrometric (ICP-MS) technique.

the development of a method for the determination of rare earth elements (REEs) in human blood serum samples by inductively couple plasma mass spectrometric (ICP-MS) technique after preconcentration by chelating resin (Chelite R).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

rare earth elements in blood serum are present at the ppt level and the concentrations of these elements in blood serum were found to be in the following order: La > Nd > Ce > Sm > Pr > Gd > Tb > Dy > Er > Yb > Ho > Tm > Lu.

the concentrations of all rare earth metals in blood serum are at the ppb level, and that the concentrations of the rare earth elements in blood serum are in the order of La > Pr > Nd > Sm > Gd > Tb > Dy > Er > Yb > Eu > Ho > Tm > Lu.
the concentrations of the rare earth elements in normal human blood serum samples are at the ppt level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concentrations of the rare earth elements in the human blood serum were determined by inductively plasma mass spectrometery after preconcentration by chelating resin.

the concentrations of all rare earths in human blood serum are in the range of 0.01–0.1 ppt (10−13–10−12 g ml−1) and that the concentrations of the rare earth elements in blood serum are in a similar range to those of the rare earths in the earth’s crust.
the rare earth element contents in human blood serum are much lower than those of other trace elements such as Fe, Mn, and Zn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the determination of rare earth elements at the ppt level is possible by the use of inductively coupled plasmas mass spectrometry.
it is possible to determine all the rare earth elements in blood serum by ICP-MS.
the rare earth elements in the human blood serum are not only the rare earth elements that are used as the medicine but also the rare earth elements from the food and the environment.
